title: COUNT: numbers only, and what it skips

screens.prompt: In B8, count how many readings in B2:B7 are really numbers.

hints.syntax: Start with = and close the bracket: =COUNT(B2:B7).
hints.func-count: COUNT answers how many numbers there are. SUM answers how much they add to, which is another question.
hints.require-ref: Point COUNT at B2:B7. Numbers typed into the formula stop matching the sheet the moment a sample is re-measured.
hints.value: The count is short. Read down B2:B7 and ask of each cell whether Excel holds it as a number.
hints.error: A range that reaches B8 includes the formula itself, so Excel answers with a circular reference.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
COUNTA counts the labels and the text too, which is the question this screen is not asking
the readings added up are 35.7, not how many of them there are
COUNT with no argument has nothing to count
the readings typed into the formula, so the count stops following the sheet
the range stops at S-04, so the 15 in S-05 is left out
a count divided by zero returns #DIV/0!

docs.explain:
COUNT answers one thing about a range: how many of its cells hold a number. Text, blanks and logical values are passed over without complaint. This column returns 3, from the 12.5 in B2, the 8.2 in B4 and the 15 in B6.

The cells that do not count are the ones worth a look. B3 holds the text n/a, B5 is empty, and B7 holds a 7 that Excel keeps as text: it looks like a number and is not one. SUM over the same range returns 35.7, so the two readings of the column already disagree.

A count that comes back short is the quickest signal that some figures arrived as text. Set the column to left align and the numbers will shift, leaving the text where it was. COUNT never reports those cells; it just leaves them out.

errors.text: A reading stored as text is skipped without a warning, so the count lands below the figures you can see.
A range that reaches B8 includes the cell holding the formula, so Excel reports a circular reference.
The range points at a row or a column that has since been deleted, leaving nothing to inspect.

docs.atWork: Importing a supplier's stock file, where some quantities arrive as text. The count tells you how many rows to fix before the file is usable.
docs.outcome: Count the cells that hold real numbers, and read a short count as evidence of text.

seo.title: COUNT in Excel: numbers only
seo.description: Six readings, but COUNT answers 3: text, blanks and a 7 that arrived as text are skipped. SUM still adds 35.7, so a short count gives bad cells away.
